visual_evidence: Four red satin-finish rectangular plastic pieces lying on a wooden table, with the top two pieces showing fractured ends
Jagged, stepped fracture surface on the top end of the upright piece (top-right) cutting unevenly across the cross-section
Exposed FDM internal structure inside the upright piece (top-right): a thin outer perimeter wall ring enclosing sparse crossing infill ribs and large empty voids
Pale, slightly whitened torn plastic edges at the raised corner peaks of the upright piece's broken top (top-right)
Semicircular hole or notch cutout at the angled, stepped fracture end of the horizontal piece (top-left)
Two additional red pieces in the lower half of the frame with smooth 45-degree angled ends facing each other
diagnosis.probable_cause: A single bending or impact load exceeded what the sparse hollow cross-section could carry, starting at the hole or notch at the break and tearing across the thin outer perimeter walls and infill.
alternative_modes: Although a semicircular cutout sits at the broken end of the top-left piece, the upright piece shows a complete fracture across the entire rectangular cross-section rather than local tear-out from a hole to the nearest edge.

solutions.title: Add perimeter walls and local infill
solutions.description: Increase the perimeter count from ~2 walls (~0.8 mm) to 5 or 6 walls (~2.0 to 2.4 mm) and use a slicer modifier mesh to raise infill from ~15% to 60–80% around the hole and midsection.
pros: Requires no CAD changes or modifications to mating parts
Uses 5 to 6 perimeters (~2.4 mm wall) and 60% to 80% local infill instead of ~15%
cons: Adds ~10 to 15 minutes of print time per bar
Requires configuring a slicer modifier mesh before reprinting

solutions.title: Relocate the hole away from the loaded midsection
solutions.description: Move the mounting hole out of the highest-bending section toward a supported end, or add a solid boss with extra perimeters around the hole.
pros: Removes the ~4 mm hole cutout from the critical fracture zone
Requires no extra print time if the hole is simply moved
cons: Requires shifting the mating fastener location by ~15 to 20 mm

solutions.title: Switch filament from PLA to PETG
solutions.description: Reprint the part in PETG instead of rigid PLA so the bar yields and absorbs impact energy before snapping.
pros: Deforms further before snapping than standard PLA
Prints on standard FDM machines at ~235 to 245 °C nozzle and ~75 to 80 °C bed
cons: Requires drying filament if stored humidly and tuning retraction to limit stringing
Costs ~5 to 10 USD more per 1 kg spool than standard PLA

solutions.title: Thicken the bar cross-section
solutions.description: Increase the bar depth in the bending direction from ~12 mm to ~18 mm and width from ~14 mm to ~16 mm while keeping the ~80 mm overall length.
pros: Keeps the same ~80 mm span and existing slicer wall settings
Increases cross-section from ~14 x 12 mm to ~16 x 18 mm
cons: Requires ~6 mm extra clearance on mating parts in the thickness direction
Adds ~12 to 18 minutes of print time per part

section_computed.basis: Same material, length and load. Weight scales with cross-section area. Bending strength scales with the section modulus (diameter cubed for a round section; width x thickness squared for a rectangle bent across its thickness). Stiffness scales with the second moment of area (diameter to the fourth; width x thickness cubed). These are ratios for the same load, not stress-concentration values: holes, notches and sharp corners are not included.

geometric_features: Semicircular hole or notch cutout directly at the broken right end of the top-left horizontal piece
Sharp external corners along the rectangular bar cross-section

rejected_alternative.visual_feature: Jagged, stepped fracture surface and unevenly torn outer walls on the top end of the upright piece (top-right)
rejected_alternative.reason: Layer delamination separates cleanly along a single flat layer boundary with intact rounded extrusion bead tops; here the outer perimeter walls are torn into uneven stepped peaks at different heights with pale edge whitening across layers.

warnings: Only 1 of 3 runs completed, so consistency could not be checked. Confidence lowered to low.
diagnosis.mode_source: Ahn, Montero, Odell, Roundy & Wright, "Anisotropic material properties of fused deposition modeling ABS", Rapid Prototyping Journal 8(4), 2002
diagnosis.summary: A 3D-printed bar snapped across its layers at a hole because thin outer walls and sparse infill could not carry the load.
